title: The second son's refusal and the Gentiles' condemnation
english: When the first son—the Gentiles—had refused, the Father went to the second son—that is, to Israel—who, being called through Moses, said, “All that God has spoken, we will do and we will hear.” But they neither did nor heard, nor did they repent afterward. The prostitutes and the tax collectors—that is, the Gentiles—condemned them.

title: The parable's point: repentant tax collectors and prostitutes are justified
english: This is what the parable wants to say: the tax collectors and the prostitutes repented and did the things pleasing to God, and so they are justified, having been persuaded by John—even though at first they were disobeying the law, or rather, disobeying God himself.

title: Words versus deeds in the kingdom
english: But the Pharisees who claim to keep the law in bare words only are rejected by God. For the kingdom of heaven is not in words but in deeds, and not the hearer of the law but the doer is righteous. The rest of these in the presence of God are like those who promised to go into the vineyard to work and did not go.
